_meta.indication: XENAZINE is indicated for the treatment of chorea associated with Huntington's disease.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 103,004 (Tetra-HD), a 12-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multi-center study of tetrabenazine for Huntington's chorea
pivotal_trials.phase: Not stated; a 12-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled multi-center acute treatment study
pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study with two parallel unbalanced (2:1) groups, titrated to best dose up to 100 mg/day over 12 weeks
pivotal_trials.population: Ambulatory patients with manifest Huntington's disease (chorea, positive family history, genetic confirmation), with a Total Maximal Chorea Score >= 10 at baseline
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in UHDRS item 12 (Total/Maximal Chorea Score), the difference between baseline and the average of the week 9 and week 12 scores
pivotal_trials.result: Total Chorea Score declined by a mean 5.0 units on tetrabenazine vs 1.5 units on placebo; treatment effect 3.5 units (p<0.0001)

key_safety: Most common AEs (>10%, >=5% over placebo) were sedation/somnolence (31% vs 3%), fatigue (22% vs 13%), insomnia (22% vs 0%), depression (19% vs 0%), akathisia (19% vs 0%), and nausea (13% vs 7%). Depression/suicidality is the key serious risk; 10 of 54 (19%) tetrabenazine patients had an AE of depression or worsening depression vs none of 30 placebo.
target_moa: Tetrabenazine is a reversible depletor of monoamines (dopamine, serotonin, norepinephrine, histamine) from nerve terminals; it reversibly inhibits the human vesicular monoamine transporter type 2 (VMAT2) (Ki ~100 nM), decreasing uptake of monoamines into synaptic vesicles and depleting monoamine stores.
modality: Small molecule (selective centrally acting monoamine depletor / VMAT2 inhibitor)

boxed_warning.content: XENAZINE can increase the risk of depression and suicidal thoughts and behavior (suicidality) in patients with Huntington's disease; it is contraindicated in patients who are actively suicidal and in those with untreated or inadequately treated depression.

rems.type: A REMS was required to ensure the benefits outweigh the risks of depression and suicidality; it consists of a Medication Guide, communication plan, a timetable for assessments, and assessments of the REMS.

companion_dx_detail: No companion diagnostic required; however, CYP2D6 genotyping is required before giving doses above 50 mg/day.

advisory_committee.vote: The Peripheral and Central Nervous Systems Drugs Advisory Committee met on 12/6/07 and voted overwhelmingly to recommend approval of the application.

orphan_indication.text: Tetrabenazine (Xenazine) for the chorea of Huntington's disease has an orphan drug designation.

citations.quote: Because this drug for this indication has an orphan drug designation, you are exempt from this requirement.

summary.text: Xenazine (tetrabenazine) was approved for the chorea of Huntington's disease, an orphan-designated indication, after review that included a PCNS Advisory Committee meeting (12/6/07) and three prior Approvable letters; approval was conditioned on a REMS to address depression/suicidality risk and required postmarketing nonclinical studies.

citations.quote: Because this drug for this indication has an orphan drug designation, you are exempt from this requirement.
In addition, this application was discussed at a meeting of the Peripheral and Central Nervous Systems Drugs Advisory Committee (PCNS AC) on 12/6/07.

In accordance with 505-1 of the FDCA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for Xenazine (tetrabenazine) Tablets, 12.5 and 25 mg, to ensure that the benefits of the drug outweigh the risks of depression and suicidality.

requirement.text: Complete the ongoing 2-year carcinogenicity study in male rats to identify the unexpected serious risk of carcinogenicity (Final Report by March 2009).

requirement.text: Conduct a 2-year carcinogenicity study in female rats to identify the unexpected serious risk of carcinogenicity (Final Report by January 2013).

requirement.text: Conduct a nonclinical toxicity study of fertility and early embryonic development (to implantation) to identify the unexpected serious risk of adverse effects on reproduction.

citations.quote: Conduct a nonclinical toxicity study of fertility and early embryonic development (to implantation) to identify the unexpected serious risk of adverse effects on reproduction.

requirement.text: Submit in vivo metabolism data in the animal species used in the nonclinical (reproductive toxicology and carcinogenicity) studies of tetrabenazine.

citations.quote: Submit *in vivo* metabolism data in the animal species used in the nonclinical studies of tetrabenazine, particularly the reproductive toxicology and the carcinogenicity studies.

requirement.text: Conduct a neurotoxicity study of tetrabenazine using methodology and a multiple dose regimen similar to Satou et al. (2001).

citations.quote: Conduct a neurotoxicity study of tetrabenazine using methodology and a multiple dose regimen similar to Satou T et al. *Exp Toxicol Pathol* 53(4):303-308, 2001.

requirement.text: Conduct an in vitro metabolism study to characterize the inhibitory effect of tetrabenazine, alpha-HTBZ, and beta-HTBZ on CYP2B6.
